title: Add additional high-priority periodicals (one at a time)
description:
Umbrella for extending the periodicals registry beyond Documentation Review, per the LIN-315 plan: add high-priority periodicals one at a time, running and assessing each as it lands. Each new periodical becomes its own child task here when picked up.

Candidates (from LIN-315):

* Corrective code-quality set: Test Coverage Gap, Dependency Vulnerability Scan, Secrets Scan, Dead Code Sweep, Duplication, Complexity Hotspot, etc.
* Advisory product/UX/business register — needs advisory mode wired first (deferred in LIN-341).

Blocked by the verify/compare subtask: validate the generation pattern via the compare→tweak loop before replicating it across many templates. (Soft ordering.)

---

# Research — next periodical (re-grounded at HEAD `b86c40c`)

Full evidence, candidate scoring, and sources are in the **exploration-notes comment**. Conclusion below.

## Recommended next periodical: **Test Coverage Gap Review** (corrective)

**Why this one, grounded in project history/state:**

1. **The project named this blind spot itself.** LIN-345 shipped a real bug through an *uncovered path* and asked "why did our tests not catch this?"; LIN-258 adds a test-coverage check to review. Testing rigor is a recurring, documented concern — exactly the "history and state" signal John pointed to.
2. **Highest leverage for an AI-agent-built codebase.** Periodicals/dispatch are dogfooded on this repo; agents generate code fast, and tests are the correctness substrate for autonomous generation. A coverage periodical is the safety net that scales with agent output.
3. **Corrective with a zero-dependency objective reference.** Node 25's built-in `node --test --experimental-test-coverage` already prints per-file line/branch/func coverage with uncovered line ranges (verified at HEAD). Fits LIN-343's corrective definition (diff against an objective reference) and respects the repo's "no frameworks / no build step / minimal deps" principle.
4. **High recurring signal-to-noise.** Coverage gaps accumulate continuously (41 test files vs 60 `lib/` modules; `tree.js` 38%, `state-map.js` 74% today), so every run finds real work — unlike Secrets Scan, which is mostly a no-op.

**Explicitly excluded:** Advisory product/UX/business register (blocked — advisory mode unwired, LIN-341); Dependency Vulnerability Scan (tiny curated dep surface, rarely actionable); Dead Code/Duplication/Complexity (judgment-heavy, advisory-leaning, weaker objective reference). **Runner-up: Secrets & Credential Scan** — recommend it as the *2nd* periodical (high severity on a public repo with heavy token surface, but `.env` is gitignored so most runs are no-ops).

## Pattern fit (LIN-343)

Transfers cleanly. The validated pattern is: a *task-generation* prompt that grounds against the repo, mints **one** cold-runnable Linear task, then stops → run → compare to a research-backed ideal → tweak `generatePrompt()`. Ship the **flat one-task first pass** (mint one task targeting the top-N highest-value gaps) — the lowest-risk replication of the validated shape.

**New shape it surfaces (defer, don't build in the first pass):** Test Coverage is the natural first **parent+children** periodical John flagged (one child task per under-tested module). Keep the first pass flat; treat parent/child as an enhancement once the flat version is validated via the compare loop. The `mode:'advisory'`/review-prior-runs shapes remain out of scope.

## "Effective with AI agents" — the ideal generated task

Must defeat **coverage theater** (assertion-free / over-mocked tests that lift the % without verifying behavior — the testing analogue of LIN-349's doc-inflation lesson and of Goodhart's law). The ideal task: targets **meaningful coverage of critical untested paths** (error/failure handling, auth/token boundaries, quota/money logic, data integrity), not a coverage number; forbids assertion-free/test-the-mock tests; prefers behavioral over structural tests; grounds in the real coverage report at HEAD; and treats "critical paths already covered" as a valid clean win.

## How it flows through LinearViewer (same as Documentation Review, zero new infra)

* **Dispatch:** the synthetic `__periodicals__` row's dispatch button posts issueless `kind:'periodical'` to `POST .../dispatch` (already null-safe end-to-end).
* **Produces:** a worker runs `node --test --experimental-test-coverage`, identifies the highest-value untested paths, and mints **one** well-scoped Linear task (default state, on the stack) carrying the cold-executor contract.
* **Consumed:** a normal pipeline agent picks the task off the stack, adds meaningful tests via branch→PR, reports via the runner's Stop hook. The periodical never writes the tests itself.
* **Registry:** add a 2nd entry to `PERIODICALS` in `lib/periodicals.js` (`id:'test-coverage-gap'`, `mode:'corrective'`, `generateTestCoverageGapPrompt()`). `buildPeriodicalNodes()` already `.map()`s the registry, so the group renders both rows with no render/tree/dispatch change.

## Prerequisites

None blocking. Periodicals v1 mechanism (LIN-340) + Documentation Review (LIN-341) are merged and author-accepted; the LIN-343 pattern is validated; LIN-349 (quality layer) is Done. Advisory mode is *not* required for this corrective periodical.

## Suggested child task

**Title:** `Add Test Coverage Gap periodical (corrective) — first pass + verify/compare`

**Framing:** Add a second corrective periodical, Test Coverage Gap Review, to `lib/periodicals.js`, following the validated LIN-342/343 generation pattern. Write `generateTestCoverageGapPrompt()` as a *task-generation* prompt: orient in the repo, run the native coverage report (`node --test --experimental-test-coverage`), identify the highest-value untested paths (weighted toward error handling, auth/token boundaries, quota/money logic, data integrity), and mint ONE cold-runnable Linear task whose description directs an executor to add *meaningful* tests (explicitly forbidding coverage-theater) via branch→PR — then stop. Register it as the 2nd `PERIODICALS` entry (`mode:'corrective'`). Then run it, capture the generated task, compare against the research-backed ideal (coverage of critical paths, no coverage-theater, behavioral over structural, grounded at HEAD, clean-result-is-a-win), and feed gaps back into the prompt. Keep the prompt general/no-hard-coded-surfaces, mirroring the Documentation Review discipline.

## Surface Assessment

**Surface Assessment: yes, implementation can land cleanly** — purely additive to `lib/periodicals.js` (a new `generateTestCoverageGapPrompt()` + one registry entry). `buildPeriodicalNodes()`, the synthetic-group injection (`server.js`), render, dispatch, and the workspace flag are all already multi-entry-capable (the registry is already `.map()`-ed; the group renders N rows). The objective reference needs **no new dependency** — `node --test --experimental-test-coverage` is built in (verified at HEAD on Node 25). Two small, expected test touches (not a refactor): `tests/unit/periodicals.test.js:13` asserts `PERIODICALS.length === 1` and `:17` asserts the single entry is Documentation Review — both must be updated for a second entry; add a `stays general` + structural test for the new prompt mirroring the Documentation Review ones (`buildPeriodicalNodes()`'s `nodes.length === PERIODICALS.length` test auto-adapts). No dispatch/tree/render/feature-flag refactor required.

nodes.body:
Note: follow the pattern we established in [LIN-343](https://linear.app/linearviewer/issue/LIN-343/verify-generated-documentation-review-task-vs-research-backed-ideal). Make a good first pass, run it, and compare what it generates against what the research and evidence shows is effective, especially with ai agents.

Larger tasks may end up making a ticket with child tickets. Some tasks will run by checking previous runs, and closing any gaps/reviewing changes/reviewing impact.

The role of periodicals and how they will flow/be processed best through LinearViewer should be carefully thought through.
The history and state of this project offer key clues to what's valuable here.

# Exploration notes — which periodical next (LIN-344)

## Re-grounding (staleness check)
- **HEAD `b86c40c`** (= LIN-349, the latest periodicals change). `git log --since=2026-06-08 -- lib/periodicals.js lib/feature-defaults.js lib/workspace-preferences.js lib/render.js lib/tree.js routes/dispatch.js server.js` → no changes after HEAD; the ticket's account of the code is accurate at HEAD.
- Full history of `lib/periodicals.js` = 4 commits (LIN-341 v1 behind flag → LIN-342 dispatch=task-generation → LIN-343 cold-hand-off rewrite → LIN-349 drift+quality fold). I re-read `generateDocumentationReviewPrompt()` + `PERIODICALS` + `buildPeriodicalNodes()` at HEAD — registry is a single `corrective` entry, `buildPeriodicalNodes()` already `.map()`s the whole registry, dispatch is issueless `kind:'periodical'`. No drift to reconcile.

## Built on sibling work (read, not re-derived)
- **LIN-342 (Done)** — dispatch = task-generation (mint one task, stop).
- **LIN-343 (Done)** — the run→compare→tweak loop + the corrective-vs-advisory bright line (*corrective = diff against an objective reference; advisory = diff against intent/goals, human-in-loop*). This is the pattern to replicate.
- **LIN-349 (Done)** — folded a *quality* layer into the Documentation periodical, reframing quality as **defect-shaped + subtractively fixable** to avoid inflation. Its quantity-vs-quality lesson transfers directly to test coverage (see Q2).
- **LIN-345 (Done)** — fixed issueless dispatch; dispatch is stable and not a constraint.

## Project-state evidence (John: "the history and state offer key clues")
1. **The project named its own testing blind spot.** LIN-345 was a real bug shipped through an *uncovered path*; the ticket itself asks "why did our tests (eg e2e tests) not catch this?". LIN-258 (active branch `wardrox/lin-258-review-should-check-tests`) adds a test-level coverage check to review. Testing rigor is a recurring, documented concern.
2. **This is an AI-agent-built codebase** (periodicals/dispatch dogfooded on itself). Agents generate code fast; tests are the correctness substrate for autonomous generation — the highest-leverage corrective safety net.
3. **Measurable gaps exist now.** 41 unit-test files vs 60 `lib/*.js` modules (+ routes, server.js, public). Native coverage already reports large holes, e.g. `tree.js` 38.75% line / 0% funcs, `state-map.js` 73.85%.
4. **Objective reference needs ZERO new dependency.** Node 25's built-in `node --test --experimental-test-coverage` already prints a per-file line/branch/func report with uncovered line ranges (verified at HEAD). This keeps it corrective AND respects the repo's "no frameworks, no build step, minimal deps" principle.
5. History theme tally (last 80 subjects): `fix` and `review` dominate — a maintenance/quality-driven project, the natural home for a coverage periodical.

## Candidate scoring (corrective set only — advisory register is blocked: advisory mode deferred in LIN-341)
| Candidate | Objective ref? | Value for THIS project | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Test Coverage Gap** | Yes — native coverage report | Highest: directly answers LIN-345/LIN-258 pain; safety net for agent-written code; every run finds real work | **CHOSEN** |
| Secrets & Credential Scan | Yes — secret patterns | High *severity* (public repo, heavy token surface, agents commit) but `.env` is gitignored + basics in place → mostly no-op runs | **Runner-up → 2nd periodical** |
| Dependency Vulnerability Scan | Yes — `npm audit` | Low: 11 curated runtime deps, deliberately tiny surface; rarely actionable | Defer |
| Dead Code / Duplication / Complexity | Weak — judgment on "dead"/"too complex" | Maintainability, but advisory-leaning + weaker objective reference than coverage | Later |
| Advisory product/UX/business register | n/a | Blocked — advisory mode unwired (LIN-341) | Out (prereq unmet) |

## Sources — "effective with AI agents" for a coverage periodical
The dominant agent failure mode is **coverage theater**: assertion-free or over-mocked tests that lift the % without verifying behavior (the testing analogue of LIN-349's "don't write *more* docs" inflation, and of Goodhart's law — coverage % as a target stops being a good measure). Grounded in the same agent-execution prior art LIN-343 already cited (arXiv 2509.18970 on agent hallucination → ground every claim; Addy Osmani agent-spec analysis → explicit success criteria, never-touch boundaries, self-verification) plus the well-known line-vs-branch-vs-mutation coverage distinction. The ideal generated task therefore targets **meaningful coverage of critical untested paths** (error/failure handling, auth/token boundaries, money/quota logic, data integrity), forbids coverage-theater, prefers behavioral over structural tests, grounds in the real coverage report at HEAD, and treats "critical paths already covered" as a valid clean win.

Minted child **[LIN-351]** — *Add Test Coverage Gap periodical (corrective) — first pass + verify/compare* — per the exploration notes and Surface Assessment above. It carries the parent's "Suggested child task" framing verbatim plus cold-runnable carry-over notes (LIN-343 run→compare loop, `node --test --experimental-test-coverage` as the objective reference, defeat-coverage-theater ideal, single-surface Surface Assessment, out-of-scope list). Re-grounded at HEAD `b86c40c` before minting: `PERIODICALS` is still a single-entry array, `buildPeriodicalNodes()` still `.map()`s the whole registry, and `tests/unit/periodicals.test.js:13`/`:17` still encode the single-entry assumption — so the drafted framing stands unchanged (one note added: registry entries use the `generatePrompt` key, not `generate`).

Parent LIN-344 stays open as the umbrella; the next periodical (runner-up: Secrets & Credential Scan) will be minted as a separate child once Test Coverage Gap has landed and been assessed. Not pre-minting it now — the "one at a time" discipline is the whole point of this ticket.

## Next child minted — LIN-352 (Secrets & Credential Scan, corrective)

**[LIN-352](https://linear.app/linearviewer/issue/LIN-352) — "Add Secrets & Credential Scan periodical (corrective) — first pass + verify/compare"** is now the second child under this umbrella, following the LIN-351 framing shape and the LIN-342/343 run→compare→tweak pattern.

**Re-grounded at HEAD `fed9c6a`** (not the ticket prose):
- `PERIODICALS` now holds **2 entries** (`documentation-review` + `test-coverage-gap`) after LIN-351 — the new entry will be the 3rd.
- `buildPeriodicalNodes()` still `.map()`s the whole registry; dispatch is still issueless `kind:'periodical'`; registry key is `generatePrompt` (not `generate`). So the addition stays purely additive — no dispatch/tree/render/flag changes.
- Registry-length/identity assertions live in `tests/unit/periodicals.test.js` (length `=== 2` at ~line 13; id/title/mode block ~17-32); the e2e spec already scopes counts to the Documentation Review node, so it won't break. LIN-352's Surface Assessment captures these as expected touches (with a note to re-confirm line numbers before editing).

**LIN-351 outcome checked & lesson folded in:** LIN-351 shipped clean (PR #363 merged, CI green — 1249/1249 unit + 4 E2E shards + `ci-success`) and was author-accepted. Its surfaced lesson was a *periodical-specific grounding trap* ("zero-coverage modules are invisible in the coverage table"). The transferable meta-lesson — **name the periodical's own grounding trap explicitly in the prompt** — is folded into LIN-352's framing: its named trap is that a working-tree-only scan misses secrets that live in git history, so the prompt directs scanning history, not just HEAD.

**Runner-up still confirmed at HEAD:** `.env` remains gitignored (only `.env.example` is tracked) and the token surface is still heavy (Linear OAuth/PAT, OpenRouter OAuth, proxy tokens, dispatch tokens, free-tier key, session secret — ~36 lib/routes files touch token/secret/key/Bearer). High severity floor on a public repo holds; no sibling task has absorbed the concern. No swap warranted — Secrets & Credential Scan stays the pick.

**Objective reference** named in LIN-352 (per the corrective definition): `git grep` / `git log -p` over the git-tracked surface (working tree **and** history) matched against a curated high-confidence secret-pattern set the periodical derives from the repo's own token formats at run time — consistent with the repo's *no new deps / built-in tooling* principle (no gitleaks/trufflehog). **Defeat-theater** mode forbidden in the generated task's contract: *report-cleaning theater* (silencing/allowlisting/tree-only-deletion to clean the report instead of removing-from-tracked-content + rotating/revoking the credential). "No real secrets found" is a valid clean win.

**One-at-a-time discipline reaffirmed:** no further periodicals pre-minted. The next candidate (after Secrets & Credential Scan lands and is assessed) — Dependency Vulnerability Scan / Dead Code / Duplication / Complexity, advisory register still blocked on LIN-341 — will be chosen *then*, re-grounded fresh. This umbrella stays **In Progress**.
